Why Not Just Use Accuracy?

With 16.1% minority class (attrition=1), a model that always predicts Stayed would achieve 83.9% accuracy. This is why accuracy alone is misleading for imbalanced classification.

PR-AUC (0.5983) is the primary metric: it measures the trade-off between precision and recall on the minority class specifically, independent of the majority class size.

Logistic Regression wins on this 1,470-row dataset — consistent with literature: on small structured HR data, regularised linear models often outperform high-capacity ensembles (RF, XGBoost).

Fairness Audit
Post-hoc diagnostic: Age, Gender, MaritalStatus were EXCLUDED from model training
This is a post-hoc diagnostic analysis only. No legal compliance is claimed. Disparities reflect dataset characteristics, not model-induced bias. The IBM dataset is synthetic.
By Gender
By Marital Status
By Age Band
Key Fairness Finding

Age <30 employees have the highest actual attrition (27.9%) but the lowest Top-50 XERL selection rate — because younger employees have lower salaries, so cost-weighted ranking systematically deprioritises them despite high risk.

Conversely, Age 50+ employees have moderate attrition (13.3%) but the highest selection rate (6.94%) due to salary-inflated ERL. This is the central fairness tension in cost-weighted HR prioritisation frameworks.

Research implication: any cost-weighted retention framework must explicitly acknowledge and report this age-salary interaction to avoid inadvertent age-based selection patterns.
